sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the only path segment of the matching endpoint. The list step converts the isCompleted and isStarted booleans to the 1 and 0 TestRail reads and sends neither when they are absent. The reads and the two writes parse against MilestoneSchema; the delete passes no schema and resolves with no value. No payload is parsed by a public method, so every milestone payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

AddMilestonePayloadSchema requires name and accepts description, due_on, start_on, parent_id and refs. UpdateMilestonePayloadSchema makes name optional and adds the is_completed and is_started booleans. parent_id is a plain optional number in both: it admits no null, so detaching a sub-milestone is not reachable through this driver.
The shared executor issues the page request with the caller's controls, and the all helper walks the envelope's next link under the supplied bounds.
The aggregate bounds maxItems, maxPages, maxBytes and maxDurationMs stop the walk and are never serialized upstream.
Query parameters are appended path-style after the endpoint token, each value percent encoded.

get_milestones takes is_completed and is_started, each 1 or 0, plus limit and offset from TestRail 6.7. add_milestone requires name and accepts description, due_on, start_on, parent_id and refs, with parent_id from TestRail 5.3 and refs from 6.4. update_milestone supports partial updates; its own table lists is_completed, is_started, parent_id and start_on, while the endpoint accepts the add fields too. Deleting a milestone cannot be undone. No field is documented as clearable by null.

input_policy.notes: Both filters are booleans at this boundary and reach TestRail as 1 or 0. The driver also accepts the deprecated numeric spellings, which are not exposed, so the numeric form is refused here rather than quietly accepted as a second way to say the same thing.

outer_result.notes: Page mode returns the driver's decoded page and all mode the collected array; entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown query field rather than dropping it and widening the result.
Reject an unknown adapter control rather than ignoring it.
Reject a control belonging to the other call mode, rather than accepting it and never using it.

parameters.semantics: The project whose entries are listed. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.

parameters.semantics: Whether completed or open milestones are listed. Taken as a boolean here and converted by the driver to the 1 or 0 TestRail reads; omitting it sends no filter, which is not the same as sending either value. The driver also accepts a deprecated numeric spelling of this filter, which is not exposed: one name for one filter is one thing to keep true.

wire.encoding: is_completed=1 for true and is_completed=0 for false, appended path-style before is_started.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the isCompleted option.
Accept false and send is_completed=0, which is a filter rather than the absence of one.
Reject the numeric spelling TestRail uses on the wire, which is the driver's deprecated alias rather than this boundary's input.
Send no filter when the caller did not supply one.

parameters.semantics: Whether started or upcoming milestones are listed, supported on TestRail 5.3 or later. Taken as a boolean here and converted by the driver to the 1 or 0 TestRail reads; omitting it sends no filter, which is not the same as sending either value. The driver also accepts a deprecated numeric spelling of this filter, which is not exposed: one name for one filter is one thing to keep true.

wire.encoding: is_started=1 for true and is_started=0 for false, appended path-style after is_completed.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the isStarted option.
Accept false and send is_started=0, which is a filter rather than the absence of one.
Reject the numeric spelling TestRail uses on the wire, which is the driver's deprecated alias rather than this boundary's input.
Send no filter when the caller did not supply one.
